encounters.cc: presents to the transplant medicine clinic for routine follow-up

lines: He presents to the transplant medicine clinic for routine follow-up
- End-stage renal disease secondary to hypertensive nephrosclerosis
He underwent a cadaveric renal transplant 5 years ago for end-stage renal disease due to hypertensive nephrosclerosis.
His course since transplantation has been complicated by several rejection episodes, one of which required the use of high-dose cyclophosphamide.
At that time, he developed severe hematuria and suprapubic discomfort, ultimately diagnosed as hemorrhagic cystitis.
He was treated with aggressive hydration and mesna, which allowed him to continue receiving the medication without recurrence of bladder toxicity.
Since then, his care team has continued to use careful dosing strategies and prophylaxis whenever cyclophosphamide is indicated.
Despite the many hours spent fishing, he maintains adherence to his medications, which include immunosuppressants and prophylactic antibiotics.
Family history is notable for hypertension in both parents.
The patient describes himself as an avid fisherman.
He recalls competing in regional bass tournaments throughout his 20s and 30s, even briefly traveling across state lines for professional competitions.
Although he no longer competes professionally, he still goes fishing 2–3 times per week and often brings along family and friends.
He jokes that most of his “therapy” comes from quiet mornings at the lake rather than hospital visits.
He denies alcohol use and has quit smoking.
He denies current hematuria, dysuria, or frequency.
He reports no recent fevers, chills, or night sweats.
His review of systems is otherwise unremarkable.
Blood pressure is 128/82 mmHg, pulse 76/min, and respirations 14/min.
On exam, he appears healthy and in no acute distress.
Heart and lung exams are normal.
Abdominal exam shows a well-healed surgical scar with no tenderness or organomegaly.
Laboratory evaluation today shows normal serum creatinine, electrolytes, and complete blood count.

He reports a 2-week history of hand tremors, increased thirst, and frequent urination.

Smoking: Former smoker, quit 5 years ago.

The patient is a 55-year-old male status post deceased-donor kidney transplantation who returns to the transplant clinic for follow-up, having previously presented in July 2020 with calcineurin inhibitor toxicity and in March 2020 with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus.
He reports a 3-month history of worsening hypertension despite compliance with a regimen of hydrochlorothiazide and amlodipine.
Recently, he has noticed a decrease in his urine output and an increase in his serum creatinine from 1.2 mg/dL to 1.9 mg/dL over the past two months.
- End-stage renal disease secondary to hypertensive nephrosclerosis
Hydrochlorothiazide, amlodipine, prednisone, tacrolimus, and mycophenolate mofetil
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 5 years ago.
3/6 systolic murmur best heard over the right upper quadrant of the abdomen.
The remainder of the examination is unremarkable.

encounters.cc: new-onset dry cough, shortness of breath on exertion, and low-grade fever for the past week

lines: New-onset dry cough, shortness of breath on exertion, and low-grade fever for the past week

This 56-year-old kidney transplant recipient with prior rejection and calcineurin inhibitor toxicity presents with a new-onset dry cough, shortness of breath on exertion, and a low-grade fever for the past week.
He denies any recent travel or sick contacts.
- End-stage renal disease secondary to hypertensive nephrosclerosis
2 months after receiving a kidney transplant
He has been on immunosuppressive therapy with tacrolimus, mycophenolate mofetil, and prednisone.
He reports adherence to his medications, including prophylactic oral trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and valganciclovir.
Smoking: Former smoker, quit 5 years ago.
His temperature is 37.8°C, blood pressure is 135/85 mmHg, pulse is 88 beats per minute, and respiratory rate is 20 breaths per minute.
Oxygen saturation is 94% on room air.
Physical examination reveals bilateral crackles at the lung bases.
- Arterial blood gas on room air:
Chest X-ray shows diffuse interstitial infiltrates.

encounters.cc: 10 days of progressively worsening cough, fever, and weight loss

lines: 10 days of progressively worsening cough, fever, and weight loss
This 56-year-old kidney transplant recipient with prior Pneumocystis pneumonia reports dull headaches for the past week and occasional difficulty concentrating.
- End-stage renal disease secondary to hypertensive nephrosclerosis
He has been compliant with his immunosuppressive regimen, including tacrolimus and prednisone.
He does not smoke and has no recent travel or known sick contacts.
On examination, temperature is 38.4°C (101.1°F), and respiratory rate is mildly elevated.
Lungs show crackles at the right upper lobe. Neurologic exam is nonfocal.
Sputum Gram stain shows Nocardia spp .
A chest x-ray shows a cavitary lesion in the right upper lobe.
Brain MRI reveals a solitary ring-enhancing lesion in the frontal lobe.

encounters.cc: Over the past 8 months, progressive fatigue, decreased exercise tolerance, and ankle swelling

lines: Over the past 8 months, progressive fatigue, decreased exercise tolerance, and ankle swelling
The patient is a 60-year-old male with end-stage renal disease status post deceased-donor kidney transplantation and history of calcineurin inhibitor nephrotoxicity who returns for follow-up.
His blood pressure has become more difficult to control despite being on multiple antihypertensives.
- End-stage renal disease secondary to hypertensive nephrosclerosis
He has been maintained on tacrolimus, mycophenolate, and prednisone
He admits to occasional lapses in medication adherence
He denies fever, dysuria, hematuria, or abdominal pain
Laboratory studies reveal a gradual increase in serum creatinine and mild proteinuria
Ultrasound of the transplanted kidney shows asymmetrically small size with loss of corticomedullary differentiation
A biopsy demonstrates fibrotic thickening of the vascular intima with mononuclear infiltrates and interstitial fibrosis
Despite optimization of immunosuppressive therapy, his renal function continues to decline
